content.title: Everything that happened in the men’s March Madness 2026 first round: Live updates and analysis
content.text: Follow live coverage of the first two days of the NCAA Tournament UConn's Tarris Reed has 31 points and 27 rebounds tonight. Getty ImagesMen’s March Madness first round — Latest The first round of the NCAA Tournament is complete, and we will turn our attention to the second round this weekend. Florida, Arizona, Iowa State, UConn, Virginia, Kansas, Purdue, Alabama and St. John's all advanced to the second round during Friday's action. Follow along for coverage from our college basketball experts.Get tickets at StubHubShare your thoughts: live@theathletic.comSKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementOweh writes himself into March Madness lore in instant classicWith nine seconds left, Kentucky-Santa Clara was heading to overtime after Otega Oweh’s shot tied the score at 70-70. Down to two seconds, Santa Clara was in jubilation, seemingly wheeling into the second round after an Allen Graves 3-pointer put the Broncos ahead 73-70, and the Wildcats didn’t take a timeout. Neither did the Broncos, despite coach Herb Sendek attempting to signal a referee to call one before Kentucky inbounded the ball.The clock hit zero just as Oweh’s tying 3 banked off the glass, though, forcing overtime at 73-73.It was needed.In the extra period of the Midwest Regional game, Santa Clara condemned itself to firing 3s on nine of its 10 shots, making only three, while Kentucky was able to attack the paint and outlast the Broncos behind 35 points from Oweh.Iowa State throttles Tennessee State but loses Jefferson Getty Images Cyclones star Joshua Jefferson suffered a sprained left ankle early in Friday’s Midwest Regional win. X-rays were negative, and he hasn’t been ruled out for the second round.All the details of how the Cyclones won are insignificant at this point. All that really matters for Iowa State is Jefferson’s status for Sunday against Kentucky and for the rest of the NCAA Tournament. Jefferson has been ISU’s rock this season, making second-team All-American as a do-everything forward. He averages 16.9 points, 7.6 rebounds and 4.3 assists.The Cyclones (28-7) still rolled without Jefferson against the overmatched Tigers, led by 25 points from freshman Killyan Toure, 22 off the bench from Nate Heise and 17 from Milan Momcilovic. Toure, whom some teams haven’t guarded lately, is the X-factor for the Cyclones. When he makes shots — as he did on this day (8-for-12 from the field and 2-for-3 from 3) — the Cyclones are one of the best offensive teams in the country. But it’s going to be hard to keep advancing without Jefferson, who returned to the bench in a boot and on crutches.Odom, Virginia chase off Cinderella ghosts Getty Images Not this time, Cinderella. Despite a first-half deficit and shaky opening 30 minutes, Virginia held off Wright State.Remarkably, it’s the first NCAA Tournament win for Virginia since it won the national championship in 2019 under coach Tony Bennett. And that came one year after the Hoos became the first No. 1 seed to lose to a No. 16 seed, falling to a 2018 UMBC team coached by current Virginia coach Ryan Odom.In his first season with the Cavaliers, Odom managed to break a painful cycle of early March Madness exits.Virginia ripped off separate runs of 9-0 and 11-0 to hold off a frisky Wright State squad that forced 14 turnovers and shot an uncharacteristically efficient 13-for-31 from 3-point range. But the Hoos had too much firepower in the Midwest Regional matchup, shooting 52 percent from the floor and 13 of 26 from deep, led by a 6-for-8 day from Jacari White, who led all scorers with 26 points. The Raiders scored only 3 points over the final 5 1/2 minutes. Smith makes history as Purdue thumps Queens Getty ImagesBraden Smith set the NCAA’s all-time assists record in the Boilermakers’ easy win in the West Region.Purdue had too much size, too much shooting (14-of-24 from 3) and too much experience for Queens to stay close.Outside of Smith, the Boilers did show nerves early but settled in once Smith set the record about eight minutes in. Smith played an excellent all-around floor game, finishing with 26 points and eight assists. Trey Kaufman-Renn (25 points and nine boards) and Oscar Cluff (9 points, 11 boards, a season-high five assists and four blocks) dominated the paint. Fellow senior Fletcher Loyer made four 3s and added 14 points.The Boilers will play the winner of Miami.Miami (Ohio) earns respect despite blowout Getty Images Miami (Ohio) proved it belonged in the NCAA Tournament in Wednesday’s First Four win over SMU. On Friday, the RedHawks looked completely overmatched, losing to the Volunteers in the Midwest Region.It brought the dream season to a screeching halt. The Vols shot 53 percent from the floor and 9-for-20 from 3-point range, led by 29 points by senior guard Ja’Kobi Gillespie.Miami emerged as one of the defining stories of the season, starting 31-0 to become the 21st Division I program to complete a perfect regular season. Tennessee’s size and physicality, however, proved far too much to handle. The RedHawks were out-rebounded by 17 and outscored 40 to 16 in points in the paint, finishing their season 32-2.Despite the lopsided score, Tennessee coach Rick Barnes said Miami (Ohio) “would win some games in our league, make no bones about it.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementFlorida manhandles Prairie View A&M in historic win Getty Images Believe it or not, this game was tied at 15 after six-and-a-half minutes. Prairie View A&M briefly made this a game by making five 3-pointers on its first eleven trips, but the Panthers inevitably cooled off. When they did, it was a hard freeze: Florida held them scoreless for six minutes and outscored them 45-6 the rest of the half. Florida’s size is a problem for even the best teams in the country, and it was overwhelming for a smaller Prairie View A&M side. The Gators scored an astounding 20 points in the paint in the first eight and a half minutes and 36 in the first half as whole, hardly needing to shoot any jump shots because they were generating so many layups and dunks. In fact, Florida had 15 layups and two dunks by halftime on the official stat sheet, out of only 34 possessions, and led 60-21 at the half. In an almost unheard-of feat in this era, the Gators led by as many as 18 before they had made a single-3-pointer. Guard Boogie Fland made all five of his shots in the first half and scored 13 of his 16 points before the break to lead the way. The final margin of victory, 59 points, set a record for the greatest Ince the field expanded to 64 teams, and was topped only by Loyola of Illinois’s 111-42 win over Tennessee Tech in 1963. The top-seeded Gators will draw 9th-seeded Iowa here on Sunday, and should again have a partisan crowd in their favor.The final margin of victory, 59 points, set a record for the greatest Ince the field expanded to 64 teams, and was topped only by Loyola of Illinois’s 111-42 win over Tennessee Tech in 1963. The top-seeded Gators will draw 9th-seeded Iowa here on Sunday, and should again have a partisan crowd in their favor. No word yet on whether Iowa coach Ben McCollum will call on divine intervention like Prairie View’s Byron Smith did amid an 18-0 Florida run in the first half.UConn gets past feisty Furman Getty ImagesUConn head coach Dan Hurley is never one to hide his emotions.So when No. 15 Furman hit a 3-pointer at the first-half buzzer to cut their halftime deficit to just 4, Hurley stood with his arms crossed, staring into nothing as his team exited the court.“What the f— are we doing?” he mouthed to no one in particular.His mood improved early in the second half, after a quick 8-2 run put the No. 2 Huskies back ahead by double digits.“Let’s f—king go! Let’s f—king go!” Hurley screamed this time, to everyone in particular.UConn won 82-71, but the game remained a dogfight until the final minutes. That’s when Huskies big man Tarris Reed Jr. grabbed three straight offensive rebounds on the same possession, which ended in a 3-pointer by Alex Karaban to push the lead to double digits and out of reach for good.It was the defining moment on a career night for Reed, who finished with 31 points (12-15 FG) and 27 rebounds (11 offensive), all career highs. It was also the first 20-rebound game for a Husky in an NCAA Tournament game in 61 years.Furman hung tough thanks to hitting 9 of 24 from 3-point range and 21 points each by Tom House and Alex Wilkins. But Karaban chipped in 22 points for the Huskies, and Reed’s monster performance were too much for the Paladins.That's a wrap on the first round!That’s it for the first round of March Madness action as the men’s NCAA Tournament has been whittled to 32.Let’s recap some more of the biggest moments from today’s action from our writers across the country.Let's hear from CBU coach, star Imagn ImagesCal Baptist head coach Rick Croy postgame: 💬 “I told the guys in the locker room just my tears are tears of gratitude. Tonight was just a true incredible representation of what these guys are about. They’ve been — they said they were going to do it and they did it. And that takes CBU to March Madness, and it means everything to our university. These guys mean everything to me. As long as I do this and recruit from here on moving forward, I will double down on character, double down on work ethic, double down on teammate-ship because of these guys.”And Dominique Daniels Jr. after his heroic performance: 💬 “Small guards, keep working. Don’t let nobody tell you what you can and can’t do on the court. You gotta have that mindset that you could do anything, .. the people that have doubted me up until this point, they see me now.”ICYMI: Daniels' heroic performance not enough vs. Kansas Getty ImagesDominique Daniels Jr., take a bow. Or two. Or as many as you want.In a game that looked all but decided by halftime, Darryn Peterson’s buzzer-beating triple icing the Jayhawks’ 20-point lead heading into intermission, Daniels had no such blowout loss on his Friday night to-do list.Daniels, or Dom-ination or Dom-dollar as the unrelenting Cal Baptist student section labels him, is the nation’s fifth-leading scorer, averaging 23.2 points. After two seasons putting up just over 19 a game, questions swirled around his likely migration to a high-major program that’d offer him stacks of cash and piles of brand deals. He wanted no part of that, utilizing two weeks of prayers and a water-only fast to ultimately opt to stay put at Cal Baptist under Rick Croy.And similar questions about his future will almost undoubtedly come knocking on Daniels’ doorstep this offseason after the senior guard scored 20 points in the second half against Kansas, putting the Lancers on his back to mount a comeback from down 26 points with 16 minutes to play to within six points in the game’s final minutes. Scoring on all three levels, there was nothing the mastermind of Bill Self or the talent of Peterson could do to stop one of the greatest — and rarest — pieces of mid-major basketball when he heated up in the second half, doing everything he could to get Cal Baptist within striking distance before Kansas finally iced the 68-60 win in the final minute.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementSelf praises Daniels Getty ImagesDominique Daniels Jr. is a rarity in college basketball. He has the talent to make NIL riches at a high-major school, but stayed at Cal Baptist this season after spending two weeks praying and fasting over the decision.Put his team on his back tonight to almost miraculously come back from down 26 within 16 minutes to play to within six points with a minute left.Bill Self, coach of the Kansas team that almost blew that 26-point lead: 💬 “It’s very admirable that loyalty comes to play in a way that I don’t know what their NIL budget is, but he can make more money, I would assume, if he went somewhere else.”Reed on dominating Furman Getty ImagesAnd here’s Tarris Reed Jr. on his historic 31-point, 27-rebound night:💬 “It’s been a tough week. That loss to St. John’s (in the Big East conference championship) really hurt and affected us. I feel like my faith has been the biggest thing I’ve depended on this whole season, especially in the postseason.”And when did he know that Furman wouldn’t be able to slow him down?💬 “Just watching film from the jump. Knowing what the scout was, trusing in my teammates, trusting in my coaching staff. Knowing that I was going to be able to really dominate down low and take advantage of the bigs they had and just take advantage of the paint. ... All glory to God. Thanks to my coaching staff and my teammates, just going out there, having fun and dominating. Playing with joy, that’s the biggest thing.”Hurley on Reed's performance Getty Images Dan Hurley has coached some special players in his time at UConn, but he was in awe of what Tarris Reed Jr. did tonight when speaking to TNT Sports after the Huskies’ win.💬 “That was the game. This guy, it was as dominant a performance as you’ve probably seen from a big guy in tournament history, but that’s what he’s capable of. He’s a total monster, and today he was a real grizzly bear.“With the injuries, obviously losing Silas (Demary Jr.), not having Jaylin Stewart — and that was not a 15 seed, I don’t know how we ended up with those guys — but when he plays at that level, we can win some games in this tournament.”Cinderellas becoming scarceWell, this is not an encouraging trend for Cinderellas:The NCAA Tournament went to 64 teams in 1985. Only seven times have the 13-14-15 seeds all gone winless in the first round.It's now happened two years in a row (for the first time).Another very chalky first roundIf you hoped last year was a chalky fluke, it’s bad news so far.Zero upsets on Friday, as all 16 betting favorites won.Only four double-digit seeds advancing to the second round, fewer than the five last year (two are Power Conference schools).Second year in a row all 1-4 seeds won.13 of 32 first-round games decided by at least 20 points.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementFinal: UConn puts away Furman Getty ImagesFinal - UConn 82, Furman 71And that ends the first round of the 2026 men’s NCAA Tournament as UConn survives a feisty Furman team thanks to Tarris Reed Jr.’s incredible 31-point, 27-rebound night.Now to find out if the Huskies can get star point guard Silas Demary Jr. back in time for Sunday’s game against a UCLA team that’s also dealing with some key injuries.Reed in the history booksPer the NCAA, Tarris Reed Jr. had the most rebounds in a men’s basketball tournament game since 1973. His 27 boards passed the mark of 26 set by Michigan’s Phil Hubbard against Detroit Mercy in 1977.Reed is the first player with 30-plus points and 25-plus rebounds in a men’s NCAA Tournament game since Elvin Hayes did it twice in 1968, per The Associated Press.Hat-tip to colleague Ralph Russo for the info.What a turnaround for the Hurricanes Getty ImagesMiami goes from 7-24 last year to 26-8 and heading to the second round after beating Missouri. Incredible job by first-year coach Jai Lucas.There are no rebounds left. Tarris Reed Jr. has them all.
